Marathon Petroleum fell 1.2% today as oil prices stabilized following de-escalation signals in the Iran-U.S. tension that had boosted energy stocks earlier in the week. On August 26, oil dropped more than 3% when Iran announced a revenue-sharing deal with Oman, suggesting the conflict might not escalate militarily—a shift from the previous day's geopolitical premium that had pushed the stock up sharply on August 24-26.

The broader backdrop remains complex: Europe's historically low gas storage and potential winter price spikes could help refiners' margins in the longer term, but the immediate move reflects traders scaling back the "war premium" that had inflated energy stocks. With Qatar now mediating de-escalation talks in Iran, the acute geopolitical risk that had driven the recent rally appears to be easing.
